'''Kirill Yakovlevich Kondratyev''' ({{Langx|ru|Кирилл Яковлевич Кондратьев}}; 14 June 1920 – 1 May 2006) was a Soviet and Russian [[atmospheric physicist]]. 

== Early life and education==
Kirill Yakovlevich Kondratyev was born on 14 June 1920<ref name=bio>{{Cite web|last=Романова|first=Анна|title=КИРИЛЛ КОНДРАТЬЕВ: "ГРУСТНАЯ СУДЬБА ПОСТИГЛА НАС…" {{!}} Рыбинская Среда|date=25 June 2013 |url=http://rybinskayasreda.ru/kirill-kondratev-grustnaya-sudba-postigla-nas/|access-date=2020-01-22|language=ru-RU}}</ref> in [[Rybinsk]].{{cn|date=July 2025}}  

He went to school in [[Saint Petersburg|Leningrad]] and in 1938 entered the [[Saint Petersburg State University|University of Leningrad]] to study physics, mathematics, and chemistry.{{cn|date=July 2025}}  

In 1941, he joined the Russian army and fought in the [[siege of Leningrad]]. He graduated in atmospheric physics in 1946.{{cn|date=July 2025}} 

==Career==
After graduating, Kondratyev was made an assistant professor in the Faculty of Physics. 

He later held the posts of lecturer, research scientist, professor of atmospheric physics, chief of the Department of Atmospheric Physics, University Vice-Rector and Rector.{{cn|date=July 2025}}  From 1958-61 he was Head of the Department of Radiation Studies at the Main Geophysical Observatory.{{cn|date=July 2025}}  

He was a staff member of the Institute for Lake Research and the Research Centre for Ecological Safety, and also helped to create the Nansen International Environmental and Remote Sensing Centre.{{cn|date=July 2025}} 

=== Research ===
During 1970-75, Kondratyev was a leading researcher in the Complex Atmospheric Energetic Experiment (CAENEX) project, the object of which was to study the transport of all categories of energy and all types of flux heat divergence in the atmosphere.<ref>Kirill Ya. Kondratyev, Lev S. Ivlev, Vladimir F. Krapivin and Costas A. Varostos, ''Atmospheric Aerosol Properties: Formation, Processes and Impacts,'' Springer Praxis Books, 2006.</ref> Along with determining the shortwave(IR) absorption of [[Particulates|atmospheric aerosols]].<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1364/AO.13.000478 |pmid=20126012 |title=Spectral Radiative Flux Divergence and Its Variability in the Troposphere in the 04–24–μ Region |journal=Applied Optics |volume=13 |issue=3 |pages=478–86 |year=1974 |last1=Kondratyev |first1=K. Ya. |last2=Vassilyev |first2=O. B. |last3=Grishechkin |first3=V. S. |last4=Ivlev |first4=L. S. |bibcode=1974ApOpt..13..478K }}</ref>

Kondratyev served as a member of the International Programme Committee for the [[United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change|World Conference on Climate Change]], held in [[Moscow]] in 2003, where he presented a paper entitled "Uncertainties of Global Climate Change Observations and Simulation Modeling." He expressed skepticism about [[Climate change|global warming]].<ref>[https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=ru&u=http://www.inauka.ru/false/article32643.html&ei=lzz8Suv0NtqfjAf266CbBQ&sa=X&oi=translate&ct=result&resnum=1&ved=0CAkQ7gEwAA&prev=/search%3Fq%3Dhttp://www.inauka.ru/false/article32643.html%26hl%3Den%26sa%3DG ''Professor Kirill Kondratyev: Global Warming is a Myth'' (in Russian)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512214716/https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=ru&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.inauka.ru%2Ffalse%2Farticle32643.html&ei=lzz8Suv0NtqfjAf266CbBQ&sa=X&oi=translate&ct=result&resnum=1&ved=0CAkQ7gEwAA&prev=%2Fsearch%3Fq%3Dhttp%3A%2F%2Fwww.inauka.ru%2Ffalse%2Farticle32643.html%26hl%3Den%26sa%3DG |date=2017-05-12 }}</ref>

=== D-SELF  ===
Kondratyev supported a new scientific direction — the theory of self-organization and self-regulation of natural systems [[D-SELF]]<ref>Ivanov-Rostovtsev A.G., Kolotilo L.G., Tarasyuk Yu.F., [[Pavel Sherstyankin|Sherstyankin P.P.]] Self-organization and self-regulation of natural systems. Model, method and fundamentals of the D-SELF theory / Ed., with a preface, comments and conclusion by Academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences K. Ya. Kondratiev. - St. Petersburg: Russian Geographical Society, 2001. - 216 p. ISBN 5-900786-51-X </ref><ref>Ivanov-Rostovtsev A.G., Kolotilo L.G. Method of modeling the evolutionary dynamics of natural systems / With a preface by Academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences K. Ya. Kondratiev // News of the Russian Geographical Society (Izvestiya RGO). Vol. 131. Issue 2. 1999. The release application. — 65 p.</ref> 

In 1987, an initiative group of scientists engaged in interdisciplinary research of open dynamical systems. At first, the group consisted of four people: [[Gennady Degtyarev|G.M. Degtyarev]], [[Alexander Ivanov-Rostovtsev|A.G. Ivanov-Rostovtsev]], [[Leonid Kolotilo|L.G. Kolotilo]] and O.A. Lyubchenko. Several dozen specialists from various fields of natural sciences and humanities joined the work in different periods. The SELF model with applications was published in a series of articles of  DAN, presented by academicians of the Russian Academy of Sciences: [[Alexey Tryoshnikov|A.F. Treshnikov]], V.I. Ilyichev, K.Ya. Kondratiev, N.S. Solomenko, E.I. Shemyakin, S.L. Solovyov and others. Corresponding members of the Russian Academy of Sciences S.P. Kurdyumov, L.N. Rykunov and other scientists also participated in the D–SELF project. Expanded versions of the DAN articles have been published in various academic and applied publications. Some of these works have been translated into English and published abroad.

D-SELF is a scientific field of interdisciplinary research of systems of various nature in self-organization and self–regulation. D-SELF is the initial abbreviation for a Double (dual) general process combining SELF-organization and SELF-regulation.

The name D-SELF was proposed by A.G. Ivanov-Rostovtsev and L.G. Kolotilo in 1989 and first appeared in the collection of scientific articles of the Pulkovo Observatory (Saint-Petersburg). The name D-SELF is an abbreviation of the first letter of the word Double (dual), which refers to two processes whose names begin with the word SELF: SELF-organization and SELF-regulation.<ref>Ivanov-Rostovtsev A. G., Kolotilo L. G. On the new space-time transformation of D-SELF // Problems of exploring the Universe. Issue 14: Problems of space and time in modern Natural Science. - L.: Publishing House of the USSR Academy of Sciences. 1989. pp. 228-231.</ref>

==Other activities==
Kondratyev was editorial advisor to ''Proceedings of the [[Russian Geographical Society|Russian Geographic Society]]'' (Russia), ''Idojaras'' (Hungary), ''Meteorology and Atmospheric Physics'' (Austria), ''Atmosfera'' (Mexico), ''[[Il Nuovo Cimento C]]'' (Italy), and ''Sustainable Development'' (USA).{{cn|date=July 2025}} 

== Recognition and awards==
Kondratyev was a member of the [[Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union]] and [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], the [[International Academy of Astronautics]], the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]] (1970),<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/member/4128/ |title = List of Members}}</ref> the [[American Meteorological Society]] and the [[Royal Meteorological Society]]. 

He received [[honorary doctorate]]s from the [[Universities of Lille]] (France), [[Athens University|Athens]] (Greece) and [[Eötvös Loránd University|Budapest]] (Hungary). 

His prizes include the [[USSR State Prize]] and the twelfth [[International Meteorological Organization Prize]]. 

==Death and legacy==
Kondratyev died on 1 May 2006.<ref name=bio/>
